ordering: ABBA per dataset, fresh single-processor JVM per arm
scope: Original supplied manifests: 8 targets x 2 amounts x 3 stock profiles per dataset; full v3 graphs, not all producible targets. TB before/after comparison, not a new AW-solver comparison.
measurement: Planning call only; excludes input normalization, graph construction and independent replay. Allocation is cumulative bytes allocated by the planning thread, not peak or retained memory.
limitations: Two formal samples per query per version. Wall time and allocation can vary with JVM compilation; differences outside changed optimizer paths do not establish algorithmic causality. Missing or budget-cutoff results are not proofs of infeasibility.

principles.dependencyScope: Uncut positive feedback is a fact of the immutable original graph and target. Share one identity-keyed immutable snapshot across same-graph orientations and quantity probes; projected/different graphs do not inherit it. Stock-dependent capacities, demand, and cut-specific metadata remain separate.
principles.cutMonotonicity: A cut removes refill alternatives without changing coefficients. Compiled positive feedback is a subset of original feedback, so only original positive consumer patterns need rechecking. A consumer removed by the DAG still retains its original metadata contract if a growing refill survives.
principles.ratioBound: For positive A,B,c,d and g=gcd(B,c), min(S,d*B/g)>min(S,A*c/g) implies d*B>A*c. If the largest exact d/c fails this necessary inequality, all refills fail. Retain all batches when the bound passes because saturation may reject the largest-ratio batch but accept a smaller one. Cross products use exact nonnegative 128-bit arithmetic.

profileCaveat: Separate 1-warmup/2-formal JFR runs over the original 48-query manifests. Baseline is the previous round final e3ce383 candidate recording. Inclusion samples are statistical observations, not exact time. Formal ABBA timings and ThreadMXBean allocation exclude profiling.
